The posterior costophrenic sulcus is the angle formed between the diaphragm and the chest wall. In a standard lateral view chest X-ray, the right hemidiaphragm is on the right side of the image, and the left hemidiaphragm is on the left side. If there is blunting or increased opacity in the posterior lower lung field, it would correspond to either the right or left hemidiaphragm, depending on the specific location of the abnormality.
